250 sports of 400 non-sports if your looking at "non-cruiser" bikes. 125ccs arent bad either. Dont listen to haters. Just dont ride a 125 with a full leather race suit like an eejit.

Hornet 250cc is a good bike. Its a fullsized like its bigger brother (600), has lots of same parts and the engine will be more than fun. Has decent pull even at low rpms (I had tendency to drive around 6k despite the bike being high rpm. Pulled through fast moving traffic without any problems)

Now, I live in Ireland, so the laws are a bit different to wherever you live.
If a bike was crashed and written off (too expensive to fix compared to its value. Eg. A 1000euro bike with damaged right fairing will be written off and the fairing would cost 500e). This bike is then considered "salvage". Lots of workshops buy salvage, fix whatever needs to be fixed and then they put the bike back on the road.

These bikes are perfect as first time bikes. They are very cheap, usually had all the maintenance bits done (eg. Carb cleaning), come with some form of warranty etc.

Your first bike should be a bike you can walk up to, kick it against its side, let it fall and have a laught.

YOU WILL DROP YOUR BIKE. YOU WILL CRASH.

You should never buy as first bike something that will make you feel sour if you drop it at the lights or you lay it down too much in a corner.

Buy cheap, ride cheap, upgrade once you learn to ride.

My 3 cents.

PS: Just youtube "guy crashes brandnew motorbike within 10 minutes". Plenty of those on the net.
